thought_title: The Word Who Came from Silence

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Μὴ πλανᾶσθε ταῖς ἑτεροδοξίαις μηδὲ μυθεύμασιν τοῖς παλαιοῖς ἀνωφελέσιν οὖσιν. εἰ γὰρ μέχρι νῦν κατὰ Ἰουδαῖσμὸν ζῶμεν, ὁμολογοῦμεν χάριν μὴ εἰληφέναι. [2] οἱ γὰρ θειότατοι προφῆται κατὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔζησαν. διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐδιώχθησαν, ἐνπνεόμενοι ὑπὸ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ πληροφορηθῆναι τοὺς ἀπειθοῦντας, ὅτι εἶς θεός ἐστιν, ὁ φανερώσας ἑαυτὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν αὐτοῦ λόγος ἁπὸ σιγῆς προελθών, ὃς κατὰ πάντα εὐηρέστησεν τῷ πέμψαντι αὐτόν.
pass_a_gloss: Do not be led astray by other teachings or by old myths, which are useless. For if we are still living according to Judaism until now, we confess that we have not received grace. For the most godly prophets lived according to Christ Jesus. That is why they were persecuted, being inspired by his grace, so that the disobedient might be fully convinced that there is one God, who manifested himself through Jesus Christ his Son, who is his Word that came forth from silence, who in all things was well pleasing to him who sent him.
pass_b_english: Do not be led astray by teachings that go another way, or by old myths that are good for nothing. If we are still living by Judaism to this day, we are admitting that we have not received grace.

The most godly prophets lived by Christ Jesus. That is why they were persecuted. His grace breathed in them, so that those who would not obey might be fully convinced that there is one God. He has made himself known through Jesus Christ, his Son, who is his Word, come forth from silence, and who in every way pleased the One who sent him (John 8:29).

choices.english: his Word, come forth from silence
choices.why: Lake's Greek is positive: the Word proceeds from silence. The negative 'not proceeding from silence' belongs to the interpolated long recension.
rejected: his eternal Word, not proceeding forth from silence

choices.why: ἑτεροδοξία is opinion other than the received one.
Keeps the breath image of ἐμπνέω.
Ἰουδαϊσμός is the Jewish way of life, not only the law.

anf_compare.notes: Material. ANF reads 'his eternal Word, not proceeding forth from silence', following the long-recension interpolation. Lake's Greek reads ὅς ἐστιν αὐτοῦ λόγος ἀπὸ σιγῆς προελθών: his Word who came forth from silence. ANF 'Jewish law' narrows Ἰουδαϊσμός; ANF 'unbelieving' for ἀπειθοῦντας is acceptable.

bible_refs.note: ὁ πέμψας με ... τὰ ἀρεστὰ αὐτῷ ποιῶ πάντοτε; pleasing the One who sent him

notes: 'Old myths' may echo 1 Timothy 1:4 or Titus 1:14 (Ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοις); not cited inline.
Source shows 'ἐνπνεόμενοι' (standard spelling ἐμπνεόμενοι) and 'ἁπό' (for ἀπό); reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Greek 'Μὴ πλανᾶσθε ταῖς ἑτεροδοξίαις μηδὲ μυθεύμασιν τοῖς παλαιοῖς ἀνωφελέσιν οὖσιν' matches A 'Do not be led astray by other teachings or by old myths, which are useless' and B 'Do not be led astray by teachings that go another way, or by old myths that are good for nothing.' Negation holds: 'χάριν μὴ εἰληφέναι' is A 'we have not received grace' and B 'we have not received grace.' Agency holds: 'ὁ φανερώσας ἑαυτὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ' is God manifesting himself through the Son, and 'ἐνπνεόμενοι ὑπὸ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ' keeps grace as agent. Doctrine holds: 'λόγος ἁπὸ σιγῆς προελθών' stays positive in A 'Word that came forth from silence' and B 'Word, come forth from silence,' not a denial of proceeding. B '(John 8:29)' is attached to 'pleased the One who sent him,' matching 'εὐηρέστησεν τῷ πέμψαντι αὐτόν.' Title names that christological thought. Notes disclose ἐνπνεόμενοι and ἁπό.

Source: Ignatius Magnesians 8 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Paragraph 1 Greek fully rendered in Pass A and Pass B. Pass A: captures all clauses: warning against heterodoxies and old myths (ἑτεροδοξίαις, μυθεύμασιν); conditional on living per Judaism (εἰ γὰρ μέχρι νῦν κατὰ Ἰουδαϊσμὸν ζῶμεν); confession of lacking grace; prophets lived per Christ Jesus (οἱ γὰρ θειότατοι προφῆται κατὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔζησαν); persecution cause (διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐδιώχθησαν); inspired by grace (ἐνπνεόμενοι ὑπὸ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ); purpose to convince disobedient of one God (εἰς τὸ πληροφορηθῆναι τοὺς ἀπειθοῦντας, ὅτι εἶς θεός ἐστιν); God manifested through Jesus Christ (ὁ φανερώσας ἑαυτὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ); Word from silence (ὅς ἐστιν αὐτοῦ λόγος ἁπὸ σιγῆς προελθών); pleasing the Sender (ὃς κατὰ πάντα εὐηρέστησεν τῷ πέμψαντι αὐτόν). Pass B: sentence 1 matches Pass A on heterodoxies/old myths and Judaism/grace clause; sentence 2 captures prophets living per Christ Jesus, persecution, grace breathing in them, purpose to convince disobedient, one God known through Jesus Christ his Son who is Word come forth from silence and pleased the Sender; adds John 8:29 citation per bible_refs. No omissions, additions contradicting source. Scripture: John 8:29 correctly alluded to in Pass B per bible_refs note (ὁ πέμψας με ... τὰ ἀρεστὰ αὐτῷ ποιῶ πάντοτε). Title 'The Word Who Came from Silence' names the thought (ὁ λόγος ἁπὸ σιγῆς προελθών). Notes disclose OCR: 'ἐνπνεόμενοι' (variant spelling), 'ἁπό' for ἀπό. All checks pass.
